title: Unable to read URL query parameters in Prerender Functions
body:
I stumbled upon an undocumented behaviour while working on [vite-plugin-vercel](https://github.com/magne4000/vite-plugin-vercel).
Currently, using Output API v3, Prerender Functions does not seem to be forwarding URL query parameters correctly to the underlying function.

Take the following route from `config.json#routes`:
```json
{
  "src": "^(/isr)$",
  "dest": "/pages/isr-QfOiv5trhLiUQCBvSSmPl/?__original_path=$1",
  "check": true
},
```

With the following function configs:
```json5
// .vc-config.json
{
  "runtime": "nodejs20.x",
  "handler": "index.js",
  "launcherType": "Nodejs",
  "shouldAddHelpers": true
}

// isr-QfOiv5trhLiUQCBvSSmPl.prerender-config.json
{
  "expiration": 15,
  "group": 3
}
```

Now I try to go to `/isr?someQuery=value`, and in my handler I `console.log(request.query)`, the object is always empty (`{}`).

For simple Serverless non-Prerender Functions, the query is NOT empty.

I cannot verify my claim, but I think that it was working in the past.


### `passQuery` parameter

I just saw that there is a documented [passQuery](https://vercel.com/docs/build-output-api/v3/primitives#prerender-configuration-file) option now.
I tried to play with it but I have no idea how it works. There is no example, and [searching for `passQuery` in your whole codebase](https://github.com/search?q=org%3Avercel%20passQuery&type=code) only points to the [initial PR adding it](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/pull/9388), with references to a Slack no one has access to.

Adding `passQuery: true` in my `isr-QfOiv5trhLiUQCBvSSmPl.prerender-config.json` makes the function always fail with a 500 error. This error does not show anywhere in the logs.
[I have an opened PR testing this param](https://github.com/magne4000/vite-plugin-vercel/pull/50).

---

So I have 2 question:
- Should my first use case work (i.e. have access to query parameters in a Prerender Function)? I would suspect so because the `allowQuery` option wouldn't make much sense.
- What does `passQuery` do, and how should we use it? I have the feeling that it could simplify my integration, as it seems to be a replacement for the undocumented `x-now-route-matches` header
